fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%: Sep-2027 NTM EPS ~$10.40 x 25x = $260) and FCF yield (40%: 2028E FCF ~$3.8B at a 3.5% yield, less ~$1.45B UIH cash outlay, /393M shares = ~$271). Blended ~$264.

inputs_detail.derivation: Current forward P/E of 27.64x at ~$244 implies NTM consensus EPS ~$8.83; an older consensus had 2027 at $8.13 when 2026 was $6.16 (+32%); applying ~+33% to the raised $6.70 2026 guide gives ~$8.9-9.0.

Hyperscaler capex growth forecast to decelerate from ~100% (2026) to ~50% (2027) and ~12% (2028) per Goldman; Vertiv revenue growth lags capex, so EPS growth slows from ~33% to ~20%. NTM at Sep-2027 = 0.25 x 2027 + 0.75 x 2028 = ~$10.35-10.40.

VRT and Eaton both at ~27.5x forward today, industrial products median ~17x. Base rate for infrastructure equipment makers as capex growth decelerates (telecom 2000 analog) is multiple compression, so a modest de-rate to 25x rather than holding 27-28x.

bear.story: AI capex second derivative turns negative into 2027-28 (the telecom-2000 and VRT's own 2025 pattern), orders/backlog concealment proves to be real softening, 2027 EPS lands ~$8 and the stock de-rates to ~17-18x, industrial-median territory. A recession (35-39% odds by end-2027 on Polymarket/Kalshi) and a 5%+ 10-year yield make it worse.

base.story: Q3 prints ~40% growth as guided, 2027 EPS near $9, capex growth slows but stays positive; the multiple drifts to ~25x NTM EPS of ~$10.4. Modest upside from $244, in line with fair value.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex comes in at the high end ($1.3-1.4T in 2027), 800V DC and liquid-cooling content steps up, Utility Innovation adds onsite power, and 2028 EPS heads to ~$13 at ~30x: a retest and break of the $380 May 2026 high, repeating the 2025 recovery pattern.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$150 (roughly 16-17x 2027E EPS of $9, about the industrial-products median multiple, and near the 52-week low) the market would be pricing an end to the AI data-center premium or a sharp cut to 2027 earnings, meaning order cancellations or hyperscaler capex cuts rather than timing noise. Ordinary volatility at ~60% annualized can reach $190-200 without saying anything fundamental.

reasoning: Base-rates lane. (1) The stock's own history: in 68 overlapping 12-month windows since 2020 the median forward return was +76%, and after drawdowns of 25% or more from the trailing high (2022, 2025) 12-month returns were mostly strongly positive (13 of 15 cases up, median ~+170%). This is heavily survivor-biased toward the AI winner, so I give it little weight. A more generic anchor for a 60%-vol stock is roughly ±55-60% at 1 sigma. Own monthly realized vol is 57% since 2020 and 60% over 24 months; the brief gives 66%. I used sigma ~0.55 lognormal with a slightly fatter left tail. (2) Cycle analog: hyperscaler capex growth is forecast to decelerate from ~100% (2026) to ~50% (2027) and ~12% (2028). Telecom-equipment makers in 2000 show that the second derivative, not the level, drives de-rating, and 7gc/Morningstar-type work flags current AI capex intensity as above telecom-era extremes. VRT itself fell ~65% peak-to-trough in Jan-Apr 2025 (DeepSeek plus tariffs) and ~42% from May to July 2026 on a revenue miss. Drawdowns of this size are routine for the name, which supports keeping 25% bear weight. (3) Macro event odds: Polymarket ~35% (Sep 24, 2026; volume not retrievable, the source page returned 403) and Kalshi ~38-39% (Aug 2026) for a US recession by end-2027, with the 10-year near 5.15%. That is a meaningful left-tail driver for a high-beta name. (4) Fundamentals: FY2026 guide $14.0B sales, adj EPS $6.70, FCF $2.5B, net neutral cash. The forward P/E of 27.6x implies NTM EPS ~$8.8. The sell-side mean target of ~$338 (29 analysts) sits well above my $264 fair value; I treat it as optimistic given the base rate of targets lagging in de-ratings. The fair value of $264 comes from 25x NTM EPS of ~$10.4 and a 3.5% FCF yield. Median outcome ~$255, mean ~$268; P(>= $244) ~53%. I ignored an options-implied band that one third-party article (Trefis) quoted, to stay independent.
